### Architect · Answer

Event: `b66a2adb1275279883b96c5b0de6c1cb` · 2026-09-29T10:05:10Z

> Committed c4630f0b2 on redoubt (docs: several harts are M2's, not beyond), signed off, 13 pages staged by path; doccheck 0.
> 
> 1. TENETS Harts bullet: one hart through M1; M2 (usable shell) brings several, first under one big lock. The reason sits beside it: the FPGA cores have two hardware threads each, and by M1's end the kernel's rules are attacked on one hart, so a second hart multiplies risk only in rules already attacked.
> 2. plan/m2-usable-shell.md: the Goal gains "the kernel runs user code on every hart". Remaining work splits into "The shell" (the 9 steps, unchanged) and "Several harts" (any boot hart, per-hart state, one big lock + one run queue, cross-hart IPIs/shootdowns/fences, finer locking). The attack cases join the Attack suite ("Several harts add no reach"), and the smp-spike facts go to Progress. beyond/smp.md is deleted, with its README and SUMMARY rows. One-hart residuals now point to #several-harts: kernel/README.md, memory.md (twice), memory-layout.md, scheduling.md, boot.md, todo/kernel-attack-gaps.md (twice), SECURITY.md; fpga-platform.md's link too.
> 3. Order: I recommend neither before nor after. They are side-by-side tracks from M2's start, with SMP begun first: the kernel has no other M2 work, SMP and the shell touch disjoint code, and every shell case written afterwards runs on several harts. M2 is done only when the bench passes booted with several harts too. Written on the page that way. If the owner wants them strictly in sequence, my pick is SMP first.
> 4. Node smp added: step, parent M2, body docs/plan/m2-usable-shell.md#several-harts.
